# Firecrawl v2.10

## Improvements

- **`/parse` endpoint**  -  Upload local files (PDF, DOCX, DOC, ODT, RTF, XLSX, XLS, HTML) up to 50 MB and get back clean, LLM-ready Markdown, JSON, or a summary. Tables and reading order are preserved, with full Zero Data Retention support for enterprise plans. Available in JS, Python, Go, Rust, Java, .NET, PHP, Ruby, and Elixir SDKs.
- **Lockdown Mode**  -  Set `lockdown: true` on `/scrape` to serve results exclusively from Firecrawl's index with zero outbound requests and zero data retention by default. Gated outbound paths include HTTP fetches, robots.txt, audio downloads, and media. Available in every SDK, the CLI (`--lockdown`), and MCP.
- **`question` format**  -  Pass a natural-language prompt to `/scrape` and get a grounded, hallucination-free answer back in `data.question`. Runs on a managed model chain with automatic fallback, prompt-injection isolation via XML tagging and zero-width-space escaping, and up to 100x fewer tokens per call.
- **`highlights` format**  -  Returns the exact sentences, code blocks, and table rows on a page that match your query. Consecutive sentences re-join into paragraphs, code lines wrap in fenced blocks with their original language, and table rows rebuild into Markdown tables with headers  -  all from the source page, using up to 100x fewer tokens per call.
- **`video` format**  -  Added `video` to scrape formats. Returns a signed downloadable video URL for supported sites (e.g. YouTube), with cookie forwarding for authenticated downloads and explicit Lockdown gating.
- **`/search` domain filters**  -  Added `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` parameters to `/search` for scoping results to a specific set of sites.
- **`/search` feedback endpoint**  -  Submit a rating on a search result with `POST /v2/search/:jobId/feedback`. Each accepted submission refunds 1 credit, capped per UTC day, with idempotent retries.
- **Custom robots.txt user agent**  -  Added `robotsUserAgent` to crawl requests to evaluate robots.txt rules and crawl delays against a custom agent string, and a separate `customRobotsAgent` org flag independent from `ignoreRobots`. Available in JS, Python, and Java SDKs.
- **Official Go SDK**  -  Added a first-party Go SDK for the v2 API, replacing the community module. Includes context-aware retry backoff and proper `MapData.Links` typing.
- **Ruby SDK**  -  Added the official Firecrawl Ruby SDK v2 with full endpoint coverage and v2-native typing.
- **PHP SDK**  -  Added the official PHP SDK with Laravel support, scrape/search/crawl/map/parse coverage, and a published `firecrawl/firecrawl-sdk` Composer package.
- **.NET SDK**  -  Added the official .NET SDK with v2 API support, parse, and an `firecrawl-sdk` NuGet package.
- **Rust SDK v2**  -  The Rust SDK has been promoted to the official v2 SDK with parity across scrape, search, crawl, map, agent, and parse.
- **`/interact` suggestion**  -  Calls to `/scrape` that pass an `actions` array now return a warning suggesting `/interact` for stateful browser automation.
- **PDF size cap**  -  Raised the PDF upload size limit from 10 MB to 30 MB.
- **PDF page-processed billing**  -  Updated PDF billing to reflect pages processed instead of raw page count.
- **Docker harness**  -  Exposed `HARNESS_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS` through `docker-compose` for self-hosted users who need longer startup windows.
- **Elixir SDK**  -  Added `parse_file/3` to the Elixir SDK for the `/parse` endpoint.
- **JS SDK request timeout**  -  Added an explicit request timeout option to the JS SDK to prevent hanging requests.

## Fixes

- Resolved multiple CVEs across the API and SDKs including `axios`, `postcss`, `fast-xml-parser`, `protobufjs`, `follow-redirects`, `langsmith`, `lodash`, `fast-uri`, and `fast-xml-builder`.
- Fixed branding `colors.secondary` being incorrectly populated when the LLM omitted a value  -  `secondary` is now optional and is no longer applied as a default.
- Fixed the Playwright service ignoring the caller's `User-Agent` request header.
- Fixed `screenshot` signed URLs returning stale results from cache by forcing a cache miss when the signed URL has expired.
- Fixed Lockdown requests being billed twice for ZDR by treating Lockdown as zero data retention by default.
- Fixed proxy billing for cached scrapes incorrectly charging proxy credits when no proxy egress occurred.
- Fixed YouTube transcript scripts running on audio-only scrapes and audio downloads not receiving CDP cookies.
- Fixed `html-to-md` conversion service ignoring zero data retention.
- Fixed a stack overflow in `marked.parse` when handling certain PDF outputs.
- Fixed `robotsUserAgent` not being honored by the native link filter and not being included in JS SDK crawl payloads.
- Fixed `/v1` status endpoints returning 500 on non-UUID job IDs  -  now returns a proper 400.
- Fixed empty `actions: []` arrays being treated as actions in feature flags.
- Fixed JS SDK watcher emitting duplicate events, leaking timeouts, and hanging `start()` on watcher timeouts.
- Fixed Ruby SDK unwrapping of `credit_usage` data fields and defaulted `skipTlsVerification` to `false`.
- Fixed missing negative-limit validation in Python, Java, and Go SDKs.
- Fixed Java SDK accepting empty API keys and missing async lifecycle methods.
- Fixed billing period timestamps, subscription lookups, and plan credit reporting.
- Fixed crawl-backlog timeouts being unbounded  -  now capped at 48h.

## API

- Added `POST /v2/parse` for multipart file uploads up to 50 MB. Returns a standard Document. Disallowed scrape options on parse: `changeTracking`, `screenshot`, `branding`, `actions`, `waitFor`, `location`, `mobile`; `proxy` is restricted to `auto` or `basic`. Errors with `PARSE_UNSUPPORTED_OPTIONS` on disallowed input.
- Added `lockdown: boolean` to `/scrape`. Cache misses return `404` with `SCRAPE_LOCKDOWN_CACHE_MISS`. Billing: +4 credits when `lockdown` is enabled, 1 credit on cache miss. Available across all SDKs.
- Added `question` and `highlights` to `/scrape` formats, returning `data.question` and `data.highlights` respectively.
- Added `video` to `/scrape` formats. Returns `document.video` as a signed URL. +4 credits per request. Unsupported URLs raise `SCRAPE_VIDEO_UNSUPPORTED_URL`; `parse` rejects the `video` format client- and server-side.
- Added `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` arrays on `/v2/search` for scoping results to specific domains.
- Added `POST /v2/search/:jobId/feedback` for rating search results. Each accepted submission refunds 1 credit, capped per UTC day via `SEARCH_FEEDBACK_DAILY_CAP_CREDITS`, with idempotent retries returning `alreadySubmitted: true`. Feedback submissions older than `SEARCH_FEEDBACK_MAX_AGE_SEC` (default 120s) are rejected. Search billing is now `ceil(results/10) * 2` credits, surfaced in responses.
- Added `robotsUserAgent` to `/v2/crawl` `crawlerOptions` for custom-agent robots.txt evaluation. Gated behind the `ignoreRobots` org flag.
- Added a separate `customRobotsAgent` org flag independent from `ignoreRobots`, so teams can ship custom user-agents without disabling robots.txt enforcement.
- Migrated the `ignoreRobots` org flag from a boolean to a `disabled` / `allowed` / `forced` pattern. The legacy `ignoreRobots: boolean` request shape has been removed  -  clients must use the new flag values.
- Deprecated `/v0/scrape`, `/v0/crawl`, `/v0/crawl/status/:jobId`, `DELETE /v0/crawl/cancel/:jobId`, `/v0/search`, `/v1/extract`, `/v1/extract/:jobId`, `/v2/extract`, `/v2/extract/:jobId`, `/v1/deep-research`, `/v1/deep-research/:jobId`, `/v1/llmstxt`, and `/v1/llmstxt/:jobId`. Deprecated endpoints emit `Deprecation: true`, `Warning: 299 - "<message>"`, `Link; rel="successor-version"`, and (when configured) `Sunset` headers, plus `warnings[]` and `replacement` in the JSON body. JS and Python SDKs surface these to clients.

---

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl/compare/v2.9.0...v2.10

# Firecrawl v2.9.0

## Improvements

- **Browser Interaction via `/interact` endpoint**  -  Scrape a page, then call `/interact` to take actions on it  -  click buttons, fill forms, navigate deeper, or extract dynamic content. Describe what you want in natural language via `prompt`, or write Playwright code (Node.js, Python) and Bash (`agent-browser`) for full control. Sessions persist across calls, with live view and interactive live view URLs for real-time browser streaming. Persistent profiles let you save and reuse browser state (cookies, localStorage) across scrapes. Available in JS, Python, Java, and Rust SDKs.
- **`query` format**  -  Added `query` format to the `/scrape` endpoint  -  pass a natural-language prompt and get a direct answer back in `data.answer`.
- **`audio` format**  -  Added `audio` format option to scrape responses, returning audio output as a field on the document.
- **`onlyCleanContent` parameter**  -  Added `onlyCleanContent` parameter to the `/scrape` endpoint, which strips navigation, ads, cookie banners, and other non-semantic content from markdown output.
- **PDF parsing modes**  -  Added PDF parsing modes (`fast`, `auto`, `ocr`) and a `maxPages` option to control extraction depth and OCR behavior.
- **Java and Elixir SDKs**  -  Added official Java and Elixir SDKs with full v2 API support.
- **Legacy `.doc` file support**  -  Added support for parsing legacy `.doc` files.
- **Wikimedia engine**  -  Added a dedicated engine for scraping Wikipedia and Wikimedia pages with improved output quality.
- **`contentType` in scrape responses**  -  Added `contentType` to scrape responses for PDFs and documents.
- **PDF pipeline improvements**  -  Improved PDF pipeline with better table detection, header/footer stripping, mixed PDF handling, inline image parsing, and magic byte detection.
- **Branding extraction**  -  Improved branding extraction to skip hidden DOM elements for cleaner output.
- **HTML-to-markdown performance**  -  Improved HTML-to-markdown conversion performance and fixed code blocks losing content during conversion.
- **Concurrency queue**  -  New concurrency queue system with reconciler and backfill for more reliable job scheduling.
- **Rust SDK v2**  -  Added v2 API namespace with agent support to the Rust SDK.
- Fixed Python SDK parameters `timeout`, `max_retries`, and `backoff_factor`  -  these were previously accepted but silently ignored.
- Capped job timeouts at 48 hours to prevent runaway jobs from consuming resources.
- Added retry limits to prevent scrape loops.
- Binary content types are now rejected early in the scrape pipeline to avoid wasted processing.

## Fixes

- Fixed empty responses when using the `o3-mini` model on extract jobs.
- Fixed revoked API keys remaining valid for up to 10 minutes after deletion.
- Fixed a race condition in extract jobs that caused "Job not found" crashes.
- Fixed `time_taken` in `/v1/map` always returning ~0.
- Fixed crawl status responses now surfacing a `failed` status with an error message and partial data when a crawl-level failure occurs.
- Fixed `maxPages` not being passed to the PDF extractor  -  previously, full PDF content was returned while only charging for the limited page count.
- Fixed free request credits being incorrectly consumed and billed on agent jobs exceeding the `maxCredits` threshold.
- Fixed dashboard displaying incorrect concurrency limits due to stale reads.
- Fixed branding `colors.secondary` not being populated.
- Fixed `removeBase64Images` running after `deriveDiff` in the transformer pipeline, causing diff issues.
- Fixed GCS fetch using wrong row index for cache info lookups.
- Fixed unhandled `ZodError` in `/v1/search` controller.
- Resolved multiple CVEs across dependencies including `handlebars`, `path-to-regexp`, `fast-xml-parser`, `rollup` (CVE-2026-27606), `undici`, and others.
- Hardened the Playwright service against SSRF attacks.

## API

- Added `GET /v2/team/activity` endpoint for listing recent scrape, crawl, and extract jobs with cursor-based pagination (last 24 hours, up to 100 results per page, filterable by endpoint type).
- Added `regexOnFullURL` parameter on crawl requests to apply `includePaths`/`excludePaths` filtering against the full URL including query parameters. Available in JS, Python, Java, and Elixir SDKs.
- Added `deduplicateSimilarURLs` parameter on crawl requests. Available in JS, Python, Java, and Elixir SDKs.
- Deprecated the `extract` endpoint  -  use the `/agent` endpoint instead. Existing `extract` methods in JS and Python SDKs are marked deprecated.
- Renamed `persistentSession` to `profile` on browser/interact requests (`writeMode` is now `saveChanges`). The old parameter name remains functional but is no longer documented.

response.description_html:
Located just minutes from downtown Orlando, Dubsdread features the oldest public layout in the area, originally designed in 1923 and renovated in 2008. This classic course has plenty of history attached to it as the former site of the Orlando Open, when it hosted such golf legends as Sam Snead, Ben Hogan and Claude Harmon.

Today, golfers are treated to the same beautiful scenery and challenges of the original course, including narrow fairways and heavily bunkered, "postage stamp" style greens. A full restaurant and banquet facility complete the ultimate golfing experience.

The driving range is closed until further notice.

GREAT SPECIAL AVAILABLE TO NON-RESIDENTS AS WELL AS RESIDENTS OF FL!

records.description:
The Rural Utilities Service (RUS or the Agency), a Rural Development (RD) agency of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), is soliciting Letters of Interest (LOI) for applications under the Affordable Rural Cooperative (ARC) Program. In addition, the Agency is announcing the eligibility requirements, application process and deadlines, and the criteria that will be used by RUS to assess ARC Applications. The ARC Program is making approximately $175 million in appropriated budget authority for the cost of loan and grant funds available under the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) of 2022. In keeping with the statutory authority for the program, RUS will utilize the ARC funds to assist Eligible Entities to achieve future net reductions consistent with Section 22004 of the IRA through the deployment of advanced, efficient transmission infrastructure and nuclear power supply. Available funds will be allocated for each purpose while advancing the long-term resiliency, reliability, and affordability of rural electric systems. All Eligible Entities are responsible for any expenses incurred in developing their LOIs and ARC Applications.


This funding notice advances the statutory purpose of achieving the greatest reductions as provided in Section 22004 of the IRA associated with rural electric systems by increasing the amount of emission-free nuclear power and increasing the efficiency of the transmission grid within such systems. These new sources of cooperative power supply and enhanced transmission efficiency will result in reduced future demand for other sources of power.


Cost Sharing or Matching:

For Project and System loans, RUS will finance up to 75 percent of the total capitalized cost of the Project in the loan component of a Project and/or System Award. Such financial equity may not come from the proceeds of any loan from any creditor, including insiders of the Awardee.

response.description_html:
Discord is a voice, video and text platform that helps friends come together to hang out, play games and have fun. When Jason Citron and Stanislav Vishnevskiy founded Discord in 2015 they had a hunch that multiplayer gaming would be the future of entertainment and that people would need a communications platform designed for them to talk with their gaming friends. Today, gaming has become the largest form of entertainment in the world, bigger than movies and music combined. It’s the fastest-growing as well.

 

Discord makes it feel like you’re playing in the same room with friends. Discord users can communicate through 1:1 direct messages (DMs), group direct messages (GDMs) and Servers where friends can easily gather in voice, text and video chats before, during and after gaming. High quality streaming and a seamless experience across devices lets people play and interact together as if they were in person. Almost all activity on Discord happens in small, private friend spaces.

Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming. We are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to talk and hang out before, during, and after playing games.

So if this strikes a chord, come join us in our mission! Explore our latest job listings and apply today!

response.content_html:
Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.

Creators are people who build audiences across the internet: influential voices whose communities listen to them and want to spend time together. Many of those communities already live on Discord, but our relationship with creators has grown organically. We have an opportunity to listen more closely, serve them more intentionally, and build a relationship that reflects the role they play on our platform.

We’re hiring a Senior Staff Program Manager to build Discord’s approach to creators from the ground up. You’ll begin with a selected group of creators already using Discord, build the fundamentals that serve them well, and develop programs that make their experience on Discord better. Over time, you’ll turn what works into programs that can serve creators at scale and, eventually, give new creators more reasons to choose Discord. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who can lead through judgment, relationships, and execution. You’ll report to the Director of Marketing, Player Communications and partner closely with Support, Product, Marketing, Communications, Partnerships, Policy, and more.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Build Discord’s creator strategy from the bottom up, starting with direct conversations and a clear understanding of what creators already on Discord need from us.
  • Bring together the creator work that exists across Discord today, establish clear ownership, and turn a collection of early efforts into a coherent program.
  • Define who we mean by creators and develop an initial approach for selecting and serving a trusted group across games, platforms, formats, and communities.
  • Create more than one program for creators, beginning with the fundamentals: accelerated support, clear paths for escalation, and reliable channels for two-way communication.
  • Manage relationships with important creators directly. Understand how they use Discord, help them solve meaningful problems, and build trust by following through.
  • Build a creator council or network that gives us a consistent view of what creators are seeing, where Discord is falling short, and what would make the platform more useful to them and their communities.
  • Build systems and playbooks that let a selected program grow over time without losing the relationships and responsiveness that made it valuable.

What you should have

  • A strong passion for Discord and/or gaming, and an appreciation for the creators and communities we serve.
  • 7+ years in creator partnerships, community, platform programs, marketing, product partnerships, or a related field.
  • Deeply familiar with how creators build audiences, operate their businesses, and manage communities across platforms like YouTube, Twitch, TikTok, Instagram, Patreon, Reddit, and Discord.
  • You have built and operated creator or partner programs at scale, and you understand how to begin with a selected group without designing something that can never grow beyond it.
  • Biased to ship and iterate. You can launch a useful first version, learn from it, and raise the ambition over time.
  • Comfortable leading as an individual contributor. You create alignment and momentum across teams without relying on headcount or reporting lines.
  • An excellent cross-functional partner across Support, Product, Marketing, Comms, Partnerships, Policy, and more.

Bonus Points

  • You have built a creator, partner, ambassador, advisory, or VIP program for a consumer platform.
  • You have designed accelerated support or escalation programs for influential users.
  • You have worked directly with gaming creators and understand the relationship between creators, games, and communities.
  • You have built programs involving product access, creator events, recognition, or discovery.
  • You have helped turn creator feedback into product changes, policies, or platform strategy.
  • You have built a program that began with a small trusted group and expanded without losing what made it valuable.

The US base salary range for this full-time position is $256,000 to $288,000 + equity + benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by role and level. Within the range, individual pay is determined by additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Please note that the compensation details listed in US role postings reflect the base salary only, and do not include equity, or benefits.

Candidates must reside in or be willing to relocate to the San Francisco Bay Area (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Solano, and Sonoma counties). Relocation assistance may be available. 

Why Discord? 

Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming. We're a multiplatform, multigenerational and multiplayer platform that helps people deepen their friendships around games and shared interests, and helps developers build and grow their businesses. We believe games give us a way to have fun with our favorite people, whether listening to music together or grinding in competitive matches for diamond rank. Join us in our mission! Your future is just a click away!

Discord is committed to inclusion and providing reasonable accommodations during the interview process. We want you to feel set up for success, so if you are in need of reasonable accommodations, please let your recruiter know.

Please see our Applicant and Candidate Privacy Policy for details regarding Discord’s collection and usage of personal information relating to the application and recruitment process by clicking HERE.

response.name: Nolla A-Frames Near Yosemite
response.overview:
Off-Grid A-Frame Glamping Near Yosemite 🌄🛖

Tucked just 15 miles east of Groveland and about 20 minutes from the Yosemite National Park entrance, our modern A-frame cabins offer a unique, off-grid experience for those who want a little more comfort than a tent  -  without giving up the adventure.

Designed by the Finnish group Nolla, these minimalist and cozy cabins are built to help you unplug and unwind. Each cabin is well insulated, includes fresh linens, and Rumpl blankets to keep you warm.

Perfect for couples, small families, or close-knit friends, the cabin can be arranged as either two twin beds or a king-sized bed to accommodate up to four people. Whether you’re here for a romantic getaway under the stars or a no-frills glamping basecamp for Yosemite exploration, these cabins offer a mix of simplicity and comfort.

Each A-frame is equipped with solar power for small device charging, a portable fan, and access to an odorless composting toilet (cabin 2,3) or a pottery (cabin 1) near the cabin. The cabins also have access to hot showers and flushing toilets across the highway at our sister property. It’s a true step off the beaten path and into a more immersive experience.

The cabins include a bed, shelter from the elements, and solar-powered lighting and charging. Because this is a rustic glamping experience, the cabin doors do not lock. We are located in a quiet, remote setting, and guests should plan accordingly. 

 • Cabin 1: Easily accessible for most vehicles. 

 • Cabins 2 and 3: A bit more adventurous  -  AWD or 4x4 recommended during rain or wet conditions.

Note that when temperatures in Groveland are above 90 degrees, the cabins do get quite warm. The best ways we have found to manage the heat is by leaving the doors open during the day (with the screen door closed), curtain closed, and fan on all day. 

If you're looking for a cozy basecamp that combines the comfort of a cabin with the spirit of camping, you'll feel right at home here.

review_summaries.summary: This campsite offers a cozy and convenient base for exploring Yosemite National Park. Guests frequently mention the stunning views, from sunrises to starry nights, enhancing the tranquil atmosphere. The cabins are praised for their cleanliness and comfort, though some visitors noted minor issues like cobwebs or ants. Access to clean showers and proximity to the park entrance are appreciated, making it a practical choice for nature lovers.

The campsite offers a clean and well-maintained bathroom experience, which many guests appreciated after a long day exploring Yosemite. While most found the facilities to be spotless, a few guests noted the presence of cobwebs, which could be improved. The showers, available at a nearby sister property, were highlighted as a convenient perk, providing a refreshing end to the day. Overall, the bathroom facilities were a hit for those seeking comfort in nature.

The campsite warmly welcomes pets, making it a perfect getaway for travelers who want to bring their furry companions along. Reviews indicate that pet owners had a delightful experience, with plenty of space for dogs to roam. While some pets might get a bit dusty from the red clay, the overall stay remains enjoyable. The hosts ensure that pet-friendly accommodations are comfortable for both pets and their humans.

The campsite provides a sense of seclusion and privacy, ideal for those looking to escape the hustle and bustle. Many guests appreciated the quiet and peaceful environment, which allowed for a relaxing retreat. While some cabins are near each other, they are positioned to maintain privacy, creating a serene atmosphere. Overall, the campsite offers a tranquil getaway surrounded by nature's beauty.

The hosts, Liza and Tom, are consistently praised for their hospitality and attentiveness. Guests found them to be responsive and accommodating, enhancing the overall experience. Their efforts to provide clear directions and helpful tips were particularly appreciated. The personalized service from the hosts contributes to a welcoming and enjoyable stay.

Nestled close to Yosemite, the campsite offers easy access to the park's wonders. Guests highlighted the proximity to Yosemite's entrance, making it an excellent base for day trips. The surroundings provide stunning views that enhance the camping experience. With nearby amenities and nature spots, the location is both practical and picturesque.

Families found the campsite to be a delightful retreat, catering well to both adults and kids. The cabins provide a cozy and comfortable environment, making it ideal for family bonding. The serene surroundings and engaging nature experiences create lasting memories for all ages. The site is well-suited for family outings, offering both adventure and relaxation.

sites.name: Cabin 1
sites.overview: Cabin 1 is our most accessible site, while still offering plenty of privacy and quiet. It is a short drive to this site, and offers beautiful views, a picnic table, and a composting toilet. This Nolla Cabin has 2 Twin beds, or you can convert them into a King sized bed by adding our provided planks in between. Perfect for a couple, two friends, or a family of 4 (with young kids). The cabin includes a solar battery (enough to charge your devices and more). We will provide bedding: sheets, pillows, and cozy Rumpl blankets.

Cabin 2 is farther back on the property, tucked away near a stream. You will truly feel like you are in the wilderness here. There is a picnic table and Yeti cooler provided, as well as a composting toilet, shared by Cabin 3. During the rainy season, All Wheel or 4 Wheel Drive is required to access this cabin. reviews.text: Lovely spot in a quiet neighborhood within a hourish drive to Yosemite
The site was lovely, and the hosts were very kind. I would recommend this to anyone. Very great location too, about an hour out from the park.
Wonderful hosts! Great little camping place and very affordable!

I’m always hesitant to rave about someplace I’ve stayed for fear more campers will come and it will no longer be available to book in the future.  However, Meadow View Haven was an absolutely beautiful location with all the amenities needed for me to stay while visiting family in the area.  The host(s) were very responsive to any questions I had.  I would highly recommend staying here.  Just one note: bring extra sewer lines as the sewer port was far away after finding the most level spot.
reviews.title: Beautiful location

reviews.text: Directions were clear. Good place to Camp of you are planning to visit Yosemite
reviews.title: Flexible check in time

reviews.text: Easy place to car camp before heading to Yosemite. Didn’t meet the host because we arrived late and left early but was easy to find and set up for the night. Would stay again
We had a very pleasant stay. The hosts were kind, helpful, and easy to communicate with. Everything went smoothly, and we appreciated having a great and peaceful spot for our RV. Thank you.
reviews.title: Pleasant stay with helpful hosts

reviews.text: Our hosts were wonderful and the site was perfect. Thank you so much!

I loved camping on Kiya’s land! I know a lot of people talked about using this spot as a prep/debrief launch pad before or after their trip to Yosemite, but I used it as my base camp. 

It was so nice to have a quiet space all to myself away from the insane crowds and packed campgrounds in the park. 

The drive in was an hour to the entrances, but that gave me time to reflect on my trip, get psyched with a playlist, and have my breakfast! Seeing the sun set on the way out of the park was so beautiful every day, and it was so peaceful. For context, I wanna mention that I love driving. 

About their site: I definitely overpacked, because they have water access and a power outlet to charge your devices/lights etc. There is also an outdoor makeshift bathroom for you to use which was a really considerate touch! The solar panels nearby are perfect to put things you want to keep dry under, but be mindful of the separations between panels, as rain may sprinkle down in between them. 

I felt very welcome there, they came out to check on me the first night I was there, and even gave me some recommendations on where to go in the park, and even was left a friendly note giving me a head’s up about some rain on the way so my gear wouldn’t get soaked! Very gracious, warm, and considerate. 

I would absolutely come back again, I want more time to check out not only the park but also what Mariposa has to offer. 

A perfect spot for both a couple days or spending the night when passing through
reviews.title: Yosemite Adjacent Oasis

reviews.text: Extremely sweet and accommodating hosts. Easy directions/instructions for staying at their site which is in such a quiet, gorgeous area. The animals on property were also amazing. Would definitely recommend staying here and hope to stay again in the future if we're ever in the area.
reviews.title: Perfect,little spot with great host

reviews.text: The hosts were fantastic and had wonderful hospitality. They responded quickly every time I had a question.

My second time staying here in a week. It's a great spot to get things done before going into Yosemite and out of Yosemite which I did both times. I couldn't go in at the closest entrance from this hip camp because the HWY was closed due to a rock slide, but going through the South entrance instead was fine. The host is super responsive and nice.

This is a great spot with FULL hookup in Mariposa. I love staying at places with all the amenities so I can do a full reset of the van before I head into a national park. Host was super helpful and accommodating. I'm staying again when I leave Yosemite.

response.body: # BERT base model (uncased) Pretrained model on English language using a masked language modeling (MLM) objective. It was introduced in [this paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04805) and first released in [this repository](https://github.com/google-research/bert). This model is uncased: it does not make a difference between english and English. Disclaimer: The team releasing BERT did not write a model card for this model so this model card has been written by the Hugging Face team. ## Model description BERT is a transformers model pretrained on a large corpus of English data in a self-supervised fashion. This means it was pretrained on the raw texts only, with no humans labeling them in any way (which is why it can use lots of publicly available data) with an automatic process to generate inputs and labels from those texts. More precisely, it was pretrained with two objectives: - Masked language modeling (MLM): taking a sentence, the model randomly masks 15% of the words in the input then run the entire masked sentence through the model and has to predict the masked words. This is different from traditional recurrent neural networks (RNNs) that usually see the words one after the other, or from autoregressive models like GPT which internally masks the future tokens. It allows the model to learn a bidirectional representation of the sentence. - Next sentence prediction (NSP): the models concatenates two masked sentences as inputs during pretraining. Sometimes they correspond to sentences that were next to each other in the original text, sometimes not. The model then has to predict if the two sentences were following each other or not. This way, the model learns an inner representation of the English language that can then be used to extract features useful for downstream tasks: if you have a dataset of labeled sentences, for instance, you can train a standard classifier using the features produced by the BERT model as inputs. ## Model variations BERT has originally been released in base and large variations, for cased and uncased input text. The uncased models also strips out an accent markers. Chinese and multilingual uncased and cased versions followed shortly after. Modified preprocessing with whole word masking has replaced subpiece masking in a following work, with the release of two models. Other 24 smaller models are released afterward. The detailed release history can be found on the [google-research/bert readme](https://github.com/google-research/bert/blob/master/README.md) on github. | Model | #params | Language | |------------------------|--------------------------------|-------| | [`bert-base-uncased`](https://huggingface.co/bert-base-uncased) | 110M | English | | [`bert-large-uncased`](https://huggingface.co/bert-large-uncased) | 340M | English | sub | [`bert-base-cased`](https://huggingface.co/bert-base-cased) | 110M | English | | [`bert-large-cased`](https://huggingface.co/bert-large-cased) | 340M | English | | [`bert-base-chinese`](https://huggingface.co/bert-base-chinese) | 110M | Chinese | | [`bert-base-multilingual-cased`](https://huggingface.co/bert-base-multilingual-cased) | 110M | Multiple | | [`bert-large-uncased-whole-word-masking`](https://huggingface.co/bert-large-uncased-whole-word-masking) | 340M | English | | [`bert-large-cased-whole-word-masking`](https://huggingface.co/bert-large-cased-whole-word-masking) | 340M | English | ## Intended uses & limitations You can use the raw model for either masked language modeling or next sentence prediction, but it's mostly intended to be fine-tuned on a downstream task. See the [model hub](https://huggingface.co/models?filter=bert) to look for fine-tuned versions of a task that interests you. Note that this model is primarily aimed at being fine-tuned on tasks that use the whole sentence (potentially masked) to make decisions, such as sequence classification, token classification or question answering. For tasks such as text generation you should look at model like GPT2. ### How to use You can use this model directly with a pipeline for masked language modeling: ```python >>> from transformers import pipeline >>> unmasker = pipeline('fill-mask', model='bert-base-uncased') >>> unmasker("Hello I'm a [MASK] model.") [{'sequence': "[CLS] hello i'm a fashion model. [SEP]", 'score': 0.1073106899857521, 'token': 4827, 'token_str': 'fashion'}, {'sequence': "[CLS] hello i'm a role model. [SEP]", 'score': 0.08774490654468536, 'token': 2535, 'token_str': 'role'}, {'sequence': "[CLS] hello i'm a new model. [SEP]", 'score': 0.05338378623127937, 'token': 2047, 'token_str': 'new'}, {'sequence': "[CLS] hello i'm a super model. [SEP]", 'score': 0.04667217284440994, 'token': 3565, 'token_str': 'super'}, {'sequence': "[CLS] hello i'm a fine model. [SEP]", 'score': 0.027095865458250046, 'token': 2986, 'token_str': 'fine'}] ``` Here is how to use this model to get the features of a given text in PyTorch: ```python from transformers import BertTokenizer, BertModel tokenizer = BertTokenizer.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased') model = BertModel.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased") text = "Replace me by any text you'd like." encoded_input = tokenizer(text, return_tensors='pt') output = model(**encoded_input) ``` and in TensorFlow: ```python from transformers import BertTokenizer, TFBertModel tokenizer = BertTokenizer.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased') model = TFBertModel.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased") text = "Replace me by any text you'd like." encoded_input = tokenizer(text, return_tensors='tf') output = model(encoded_input) ``` ### Limitations and bias Even if the training data used for this model could be characterized as fairly neutral, this model can have biased predictions: ```python >>> from transformers import pipeline >>> unmasker = pipeline('fill-mask', model='bert-base-uncased') >>> unmasker("The man worked as a [MASK].") [{'sequence': '[CLS] the man worked as a carpenter. [SEP]', 'score': 0.09747550636529922, 'token': 10533, 'token_str': 'carpenter'}, {'sequence': '[CLS] the man worked as a waiter. [SEP]', 'score': 0.0523831807076931, 'token': 15610, 'token_str': 'waiter'}, {'sequence': '[CLS] the man worked as a barber. [SEP]', 'score': 0.04962705448269844, 'token': 13362, 'token_str': 'barber'}, {'sequence': '[CLS] the man worked as a mechanic. [SEP]', 'score': 0.03788609802722931, 'token': 15893, 'token_str': 'mechanic'}, {'sequence': '[CLS] the man worked as a salesman. [SEP]', 'score': 0.037680890411138535, 'token': 18968, 'token_str': 'salesman'}] >>> unmasker("The woman worked as a [MASK].") [{'sequence': '[CLS] the woman worked as a nurse. [SEP]', 'score': 0.21981462836265564, 'token': 6821, 'token_str': 'nurse'}, {'sequence': '[CLS] the woman worked as a waitress. [SEP]', 'score': 0.1597415804862976, 'token': 13877, 'token_str': 'waitress'}, {'sequence': '[CLS] the woman worked as a maid. [SEP]', 'score': 0.1154729500412941, 'token': 10850, 'token_str': 'maid'}, {'sequence': '[CLS] the woman worked as a prostitute. [SEP]', 'score': 0.037968918681144714, 'token': 19215, 'token_str': 'prostitute'}, {'sequence': '[CLS] the woman worked as a cook. [SEP]', 'score': 0.03042375110089779, 'token': 5660, 'token_str': 'cook'}] ``` This bias will also affect all fine-tuned versions of this model. ## Training data The BERT model was pretrained on [BookCorpus](https://yknzhu.wixsite.com/mbweb), a dataset consisting of 11,038 unpublished books and [English Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Wikipedia) (excluding lists, tables and headers). ## Training procedure ### Preprocessing The texts are lowercased and tokenized using WordPiece and a vocabulary size of 30,000. The inputs of the model are then of the form: ``` [CLS] Sentence A [SEP] Sentence B [SEP] ``` With probability 0.5, sentence A and sentence B correspond to two consecutive sentences in the original corpus, and in the other cases, it's another random sentence in the corpus. Note that what is considered a sentence here is a consecutive span of text usually longer than a single sentence. The only constrain is that the result with the two "sentences" has a combined length of less than 512 tokens. The details of the masking procedure for each sentence are the following: - 15% of the tokens are masked. - In 80% of the cases, the masked tokens are replaced by `[MASK]`. - In 10% of the cases, the masked tokens are replaced by a random token (different) from the one they replace. - In the 10% remaining cases, the masked tokens are left as is. ### Pretraining The model was trained on 4 cloud TPUs in Pod configuration (16 TPU chips total) for one million steps with a batch size of 256. The sequence length was limited to 128 tokens for 90% of the steps and 512 for the remaining 10%. The optimizer used is Adam with a learning rate of 1e-4, \\(\beta_{1} = 0.9\\) and \\(\beta_{2} = 0.999\\), a weight decay of 0.01, learning rate warmup for 10,000 steps and linear decay of the learning rate after. ## Evaluation results When fine-tuned on downstream tasks, this model achieves the following results: Glue test results: | Task | MNLI-(m/mm) | QQP | QNLI | SST-2 | CoLA | STS-B | MRPC | RTE | Average | |:----:|:-----------:|:----:|:----:|:-----:|:----:|:-----:|:----:|:----:|:-------:| | | 84.6/83.4 | 71.2 | 90.5 | 93.5 | 52.1 | 85.8 | 88.9 | 66.4 | 79.6 | ### BibTeX entry and citation info ```bibtex @article{DBLP:journals/corr/abs-1810-04805, author = {Jacob Devlin and Ming{-}Wei Chang and Kenton Lee and Kristina Toutanova}, title = {{BERT:} Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding}, journal = {CoRR}, volume = {abs/1810.04805}, year = {2018}, url = {http://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04805}, archivePrefix = {arXiv}, eprint = {1810.04805}, timestamp = {Tue, 30 Oct 2018 20:39:56 +0100}, biburl = {https://dblp.org/rec/journals/corr/abs-1810-04805.bib}, bibsource = {dblp computer science bibliography, https://dblp.org} } ```

fields.about: Retrieval instant, RFC 3339 UTC.

fields.about: The JSON-LD dates verbatim. Some portals emit placeholders generated at request time (datePosted = now minus two years and/or validThrough = now plus one year, with a millisecond clock reading instead of a midnight-anchored instant). sections.text:
Good Shepherd Hospice is seeking a compassionate candidate for a Registered Nurse Case Manager serving patients and their families in Ft. Worth and surrounding communities.
The RN provides nursing assessment, planning and care to maximize the comfort and health of patients and families. The RN responds to all phone calls promptly and appropriately, makes patient visits as necessary and completes after hours admissions and deaths as needed.
Previous experience in hospice, home health, or geriatrics preferred

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.html:
• Receives patient assignments from the Patient Care Manager or Case Manager. Initiates communication with attending physicians, hospice staff members and other agencies as needed to coordinate optimal care and use of resources for the patient/family.
  •  Cultivates communication and
sections.text:
Receives patient assignments from the Patient Care Manager or Case Manager. Initiates communication with attending physicians, hospice staff members and other agencies as needed to coordinate optimal care and use of resources for the patient/family.
Cultivates communication and bereavement skills.
Maintains regular communication with the attending physician concerning patient/family care.
Contacts families of new patient assignment, maintains regular communication as requested or desired by family.
Obtains data on physical, psychological, social and spiritual factors that may influence patient/family health status and incorporate that data into the Plan of Care.
Maintains up to date patient records so that problems, plans, actions and goals are accurately and clearly stated and changes are reflected as they occur. Turn paperwork into office as required by Medicare and Good Shepherd Hospice policies and procedures.
Instructs the patient and caregiver:
How to administer medication, recognizing side effects, and adverse reactions.
How to perform personal care and oral hygiene.
How to assist in lifting, moving, ambulation and exercise.
Disaster/Safety Management.
How to prepare for the events preceding death.
Informs the Patient Care Manager of unusual or potentially problematic patient/family issues.
Attends the Hospice team meetings and other patient conferences, including care plan meetings, as deemed necessary by the Patient Care Manager.
Provides appropriate support at time of death.
Shares in providing 24-hour, seven days a week coverage to patients and
families.
Evaluates hospice aides every two weeks.
Evaluate LPN at a minimum of one time per month.
Through individualized studies, learn and develop understanding of hospice philosophy.
Become proficient in pain management through individualized reading, in services or seminars.
All other task assigned

sections.heading: Qualifications
sections.html:
1. Registered Nurse currently licensed in the state in which the care is provided. 
  2. Previous experience in hospice, home health, geriatrics or general medical/surgical nursing. 
  3. Demonstrated commitment to the hospice philosophy of care.

records.author: Liz
records.body: I have two Hemnes bookcases but needed something smaller for art supplies and books and when I saw the blue I fell in love! Bought a few extra glass shelves and baskets to organize my once unruly paints and pencils, power cords and electronics - my work laptop, personal laptop, Kindle and iPad are all easy to find - and it’s perfect. I smile whenever I look at my space. Thinking of buying a third just for manga and merch.
records.title: Color won me over

records.author: Marie
records.body: Both back panels on this bookshelves are damaged.  I need a call
records.title: Damage

records.author: Kevin
records.body:
Bought the larger bookshelf about a year ago and recently decided to expand my fiancées library. Got home only to notice my current bookshelf was 2-3 shades darker. Thought I purchased the wrong finish, so I disassembled everything, returned it, bought the darker finish. I got home only to realize this also didn’t match. When I talked to customer service I was told occasionally their suppliers change and there was nothing I could do about it. 

So long story short: Don’t purchase these if you plan on expanding your library later on, or if you are buying them to expand the bookshelf you already own.
records.title: Great bookshelf, but don’t plan on expanding it later

records.author: Cynthia
records.body: We had two awkward little alcoves that were wasted space. These bookcases fit beautifully.
records.title: Good choice

records.author: Betty
records.body: Was looking for additional storage for my closet.  The versatile of this storage unit was just the right solution.  It fit nicely into the corner of my closet turning dead space into additional storage.  I would highly recommend it.
records.title: Just the right size

records.author: W Thomas
records.body: Today's Billy Bookcases are not the same as the ones I bought 15+ years ago.  Color, wood pattern, and size have changed.  Nothing matches.  Why call them by the same name if they have changed?  I hope the new ones are as sturdy as the older ones.
records.title: If you change the game, change the name.

records.author: Sara
records.body: I purchased one bookcase and then quickly bought 3 more.  The verticality really helps with storage in small spaces and they hold quite a bit.  Recommend.
records.title: So good, I purchased 4

records.author: Bobby
records.body: Assembly was not difficult. Love the black oak effect.
records.title: Good Looking Bookcase

records.author: Pamela
records.body: My husband and I recently moved into a new home and bought 2 Billy Bookcases to augment the closet system in our primary bedroom. We have never had to assemble furniture before and found the bookcases easy to put together, attractive, sturdy and functional! We are now considering the Billy Bookcase cabinet system for our back entry drop zone. Great product, Ikea!
records.title: Operation Billy Bookcase

records.author: Monica
records.body: We use these everywhere, Large spaces, small spaces, they just work. They look great and I LOVE that you can add a bit of wallpaper or paint to the backing and give it all kinds of character.
records.title: What a versatile shelf!

records.author: Diane
records.body: I purchased this recently to organize my husband‘s video games. I only had a limited amount of space to put an organizer and this was perfect. My husband also loved it because now all his games were nice, organized and easier to find what he is looking for.
records.title: Perfect for small spaces

records.author: Sara
records.body: Please restock, I need another! Its so perfect.
records.title: THE BEST COLOR

records.author: Daniel
records.body: I really like the look of this bookcase, but IKEA offers no way to purchase additional blue shelves for this piece. If you want more blue shelves than what is provided, you will have to buy entire additional bookcase.
records.title: No additional shelving

records.author: Eduardo
records.body: Easy to assembly.Perfect fit for my place.
records.title: Billy Bookcase

records.author: Richard
records.body: Good construction, great price. Instruction pictorial needs some study before diving. Be sure you don't need the larger model.
records.title: Great small bookcase.

records.author: John
records.body: I needed storage space in my bathroom and the bookcase fit the spot and now my bathroom is organized and everything is easy to locate. My home has a lot of storage issues and this is one of my solutions.
records.title: billy to the rescue

records.author: Margarita
records.body:
I got 5 units to build a custom media center for my office/playroom for my son and I to have better organization. Each unit took me less that 15 minutes to build! We added the doors as well for a cleaner look (I get overstimulated easily with messes). I used the Billy tool to help create what I was looking for! 
I will say, delivery took forever so in the future I would much rather use the click and collect option and pick it up myself or just go in and shop what I need. Thank you ikea for creating such creative and amazing storage hacks!
records.title: Billy is the way to go!!

records.author: Tina
records.body: Bought the corner hardware separately. They went together easily (make sure you have a ratcheting screwdriver to avoid hand pain and cracking the particleboard veneer).
records.title: Great Shelves

records.author: Dana
records.body: I bought 3 with the corner connector kit. Top half is super easy, bottom half not so and once they're in place good luck if you need to shift them BUT! I adore the bookcases. Perfect depth for little book display setups, fits quite a lot if you're just shelving books. Addons are good too, I plan to build a whole library wall with these complete with ladder rail eventually.
records.title: Perfect for books/media display!

records.author: Jennifer
records.body: Affordable, easy assembly, and the height extensions are amazing!!!
records.title: Love this Bookcase

providers.name: Indeed US
providers.description: Indeed US job search, full job postings and employer profiles (rating, review category scores, size, revenue, industry, addresses, CEO, links) from Indeed's own GraphQL API, with the public company page as fallback and salary and location normalised.

tools.name: Employer
tools.description: Employer research after search or job returned an employer key or url. Prefer employer_key (solver-free, one GraphQL call); unknown keys and slugs return not_found.

options.name: company
options.about: Company page slug as it appears after /cmp/, e.g. Apple or Charles-Schwab.

options.name: employer_key
options.about: Indeed's employer key as returned in employer.key on search and job results, e.g. e3a48f8a4a788271. Pattern: ^[0-9a-fA-F]{16}$.

options.name: url
options.about: A pasted indeed.com company URL, e.g. https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Apple.

response.about: One Indeed employer profile by employer key (the 16-hex employer.key on every job), by company page slug (the name after /cmp/) or by a pasted indeed.com/cmp URL: name, overall rating and review count, review category scores (work-life balance, compensation, job security, management, culture), description, industry (code plus label), employee and revenue ranges (code plus label), addresses, website and social links, CEO name, logo and header image URLs. Read from Indeed's GraphQL employer dossier; a slug is resolved to its key through a company: job search. Only when the company has no current US posting is the public company page read instead, which additionally exposes founded year, headquarters, Work Happiness score, ratings by year, top locations, open job count and CEO approval; data_source names the path taken.

fields.name: addresses
fields.about: Addresses as listed in the employer dossier; empty from the company page.

fields.name: company_key
fields.about: Indeed's encrypted company id (encodedFccId); matches employer.key on jobs.

fields.name: data_source
fields.about: Which Indeed surface produced this record: the GraphQL employer dossier or the public company page fallback.

fields.name: employee_range
fields.about: Decoded from employee_range_code, e.g. "10,000+"; null when the code is unknown.

fields.name: employee_range_code
fields.about: Indeed's raw code, e.g. ERv1_10000_PLUS.

fields.name: industry_code
fields.about: Indeed's raw industry code, e.g. Iv1_INTERNET_AND_SOFTWARE (GraphQL path only; null from the company page).

fields.name: rating
fields.about: Overall review rating out of 5.

fields.name: revenue_range
fields.about: Decoded from revenue_range_code, USD, e.g. "more than $10B (USD)".

fields.name: revenue_range_code
fields.about: Indeed's raw code, e.g. RRv1_OVER_10B.

fields.name: social_links
fields.about: Employer-provided social profile URLs (GraphQL path); null from the company page.

tools.name: Job
tools.description: After search, or when you hold a viewjob?jk= or rc/clk?jk= URL. Removed postings return not_found.

options.name: job_key
options.about: Indeed job key, e.g. d6adfa9517df46fc. Pattern: ^[0-9a-fA-F]{16}$.

options.name: url
options.about: A pasted indeed.com job URL containing jk=, e.g. https://www.indeed.com/viewjob?jk=d6adfa9517df46fc.

response.about: One Indeed job posting by job key (the 16-hex jk) or a pasted indeed.com job URL: title, employer, normalised location and salary, attributes, description as HTML and text, posted/listed timestamps, repost flag, expiry flag and outbound apply URL.

fields.name: attributes
fields.about: Indeed's taxonomy tags for the posting, as Indeed returns them: skills, benefits, schedule, seniority, job type and, when tagged, the workplace type. The workplace type (key DSQF7 "Remote", PAXZC "Hybrid work", SWG7T "In-person", N83EH "Work from home") is optional: it is present only on postings Indeed tagged with it, so its absence does not mean on-site. Order is Indeed's; the list may be empty.

fields.name: listed_at
fields.about: RFC3339 UTC; Indeed's dateOnIndeed, when the posting was listed on Indeed.

fields.name: posted_at
fields.about: RFC3339 UTC; Indeed's datePublished, the posting date the employer's listing carries. For a reposted posting this is the repost date, not the original one.

fields.name: reposted
fields.about: Indeed's isRepost: true when Indeed marks the posting as a repost of an earlier one, false when not, null when Indeed does not say.

response.description_html:
At Apple, we focus deeply on our customers’ experience. Apple Ads brings this same approach to advertising, helping people find exactly what they’re looking for and helping advertisers grow their businesses. Our technology powers ads and sponsorships across Apple Services, including the App Store, Apple News, and MLS Season Pass. Everything we do is designed for trust, connection, and impact: We respect user privacy, integrate advertising thoughtfully into the experience, and deliver value for advertisers of all sizes-from small app developers to big, global brands. Because when advertising is done right, it benefits everyone.

Description

Ads Engineering builds ad tech the Apple way-privacy-preserving, user-centric, and built to scale. Our infrastructure supports massive real-time demand with low latency, precision, and global reach. Our work spans distributed systems, large-scale data infrastructure, LLMs, and Generative AI. We design and build best of breed systems for dealing with our complex and ever-growing platform needs that help deliver highly optimized advertising content to consumers.","responsibilities":"Build the foundational pieces of the next generation of Apple Ad’s systems

Implement low latency, highly - available, high volume internal and external facing services in a cloud environment.

Design and implement performant services created with the right principles to support rapid growth with minimal operational overheads

Collaborate with cross functional teams including Product Management, Data, SRE, etc. to design and implement systems that can handle a variety of Ads use cases.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree preferred

5+ years of experience in software engineering

Proficiency in Java

Prior experience in advertising industry is a plus

Minimum Qualifications

2 or more years of industry experience building scalable micro services or data driven platforms

Strong computer science fundamentals

Prior experience with OOPS programming (eg., Java/C++ or equivalent)

Familiarity with cloud paradigms ( e.g AWS or GCP )

Expertise in building backend distributed systems

Experience with creating solutions using public cloud technologies and APIs

Strong understanding of Micro-service design and high-scale performance tuning

Expertise in relational and non relational datastore

Proficiency in data processing technologies (e.g Kafka, Spark, Flink )

Strong problem solving and debugging skills

A desire to work in a fast-paced work environment

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science/Engineering discipline or equivalent

Pay & Benefits

At Apple, base pay is one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. This provides the opportunity to progress as you grow and develop within a role. The base pay range for this role is between $129,300 and $225,300, and your base pay will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, and location.

Apple employees also have the opportunity to become an Apple shareholder through participation in Apple's discretionary employee stock programs. Apple employees are eligible for discretionary restricted stock unit awards, and can purchase Apple stock at a discount if voluntarily participating in Apple's Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You'll also receive benefits including: Comprehensive medical and dental coverage, retirement benefits, a range of discounted products and free services, and for formal education related to advancing your career at Apple, reimbursement for certain educational expenses - including tuition. Additionally, this role might be eligible for discretionary bonuses or commission payments as well as relocation. Learn more about Apple Benefits

Note: Apple benefit, compensation and employee stock programs are subject to eligibility requirements and other terms of the applicable plan or program.

tools.name: Search
tools.description: Start here to find job_key values; pass the same filters plus next_cursor to page. No total count is exposed by Indeed; next_cursor=null is the end.

options.name: cursor
options.about: next_cursor from the previous page; send it with the same query, location and filters.

options.name: limit
options.about: Page size; Indeed's maximum is 100.

options.name: location
options.about: City and state, ZIP code, state, or "Remote" (Indeed's "where" box). At least one of query/location is required.

options.name: posted_within_days
options.about: Only cards Indeed listed within the last N days, i.e. on listed_at (Indeed's dateOnIndeed, the only field its date filter accepts). posted_at is not filtered: it can be older than N days, and for a reposted card it is the repost date. Check reposted and posted_at on each card.

options.name: query
options.about: Job title, keywords or company name (Indeed's "what" box).

options.name: radius_miles
options.about: Search radius around the location in miles.

options.name: remote
options.about: true restricts to jobs carrying Indeed's Remote attribute.

options.name: sort
options.about: Result order: "relevance" (Indeed's default ranking) or "date" (most recently listed first). No other order is offered by Indeed.

response.about: Search Indeed US job postings by keywords and/or location (city/state, ZIP or "Remote"), with radius, newest-first sort, posted-within-days and remote filters. Returns one page of up to 100 job cards with normalised salary (min/max, currency, period, posted vs estimated), location, employer, attributes, Indeed's own posted/listed timestamps and repost flag, plus next_cursor. posted_within_days filters on listed_at (when Indeed listed the card), the only date Indeed's filter accepts; a card's posted_at can be weeks older, and for reposted=true it is the repost date, not the original posting date.

fields.name: apply_url
fields.about: Indeed's outbound apply URL, when present.

fields.name: attributes
fields.about: Indeed's taxonomy tags for the posting, as Indeed returns them: skills, benefits, schedule, seniority, job type and, when tagged, the workplace type. The workplace type (key DSQF7 "Remote", PAXZC "Hybrid work", SWG7T "In-person", N83EH "Work from home") is optional: it is present only on postings Indeed tagged with it and absent on many cards, so its absence does not mean on-site. Order is Indeed's; the list may be empty.

fields.name: job_key
fields.about: Indeed's stable job key (jk).

fields.name: listed_at
fields.about: RFC3339 UTC; Indeed's dateOnIndeed, when this card was listed on Indeed. The field posted_within_days filters on.

fields.name: posted_at
fields.about: RFC3339 UTC; Indeed's datePublished, the posting date the employer's listing carries. For a reposted card this is the repost date, not the original one; it is not what posted_within_days filters on.

fields.name: reposted
fields.about: Indeed's isRepost: true when Indeed marks the posting as a repost of an earlier one (posted_at is then the repost date), false when it does not, null when Indeed does not say. Read from Indeed's jobData for the page, since the search surface leaves it null.

fields.name: snippet
fields.about: First 300 characters of the description text.

fields.name: source_name
fields.about: The board or employer Indeed sourced the posting from.

response.description:
Wir begleiten unsere Kunden Ende-zu-Ende - von der strategischen, KI-nativen Neuausrichtung & Zieldefinition der Organisation über die Konzeption & Entwicklung von cutting-edge KI-Lösungen bis hin zum technischen Design & der Implementierung von KI- & Daten-Plattformen. Dabei verbinden wir fachliche Expertise, moderne KI-Technologien (insb. generative und agentische KI) und tiefes Technologieverständnis, um messbaren, transformativen Geschäftswert zu schaffen.

## Aufgaben

**Das erwartet dich:**

*   **KI- und Datenanwendungen mit Vision**  
Nutze dein technisches Fachwissen und deine Leidenschaft für moderne Technologien, um die nächste Generation von KI- und Datenarchitekturen für unsere Kunden zu gestalten und den Einsatz generativer und agentischer KI voranzutreiben.  
 
*   **Technologieberatung auf höchstem Niveau**  
Als Teil eines interdisziplinären Teams identifizierst du als Technology Consultant die passenden Technologien und Architekturen, um Daten- und KI-Anwendungen effizient und skalierbar nutzbar zu machen. Du bewertest technologische Optionen, entwirfst Zielarchitekturen und leitest daraus belastbare technische Konzepte und Roadmaps ab.  
 
*   **Realer Impact für Industrien und Gesellschaft**  
Bei Accenture arbeitest du mit weltweit führenden Unternehmen und Institutionen an wegweisenden Lösungen. Das Ziel: datengetriebene Anwendungsfälle identifizieren, gestalten, testen und erfolgreich in die Praxis bringen - von der ersten Idee bis zur Skalierung. So schaffst du echten Mehrwert und treibst Innovation voran.  
 
*   **Implementierung von Lösungen mit nachhaltigem Erfolg**  
In enger Zusammenarbeit mit Entscheidungsträger:innen und Umsetzungsteams verantwortest du die technische Realisierung von Lösungen im KI und Datenbereich. Du stellst eine saubere Integration in bestehende Systemlandschaften sicher und begleitest den Übergang in den produktiven Betrieb - mit besonderem Augenmerk auf Stabilität, Sicherheit, Skalierbarkeit und langfristige Wartbarkeit.

## Qualifikation

**Darauf freuen wir uns:**

*   Erfolgreicher Abschluss eines relevanten Studiums auf Master- oder PhD-Niveau im IT-Bereich, bevorzugt mit Schwerpunkt KI, Data Engineering, Software-Engineering oder Datenbanken.  
 
*   Mindestens 2-3 Jahre Berufserfahrung in einem einschlägigen Bereich.  
 
*   Fortgeschrittene Kenntnisse in diesen Bereichen setzen wir voraus: Software-Engineering (z.B.: Python, Scala, Java, C#, Go), Version Control System (z.B.: Git, Azure DevOps), Datenmanipulation (z.B.: SQL, R, Spark), SQL-Datenbanken (z.B.: MS SQL Server, Oracle, Postgres), Web APIs (z.B.: REST, SOAP).  
 
*   Zusätzlich erwarten wir uns Expertise in einem der folgenden Kernbereiche:  
\- Advanced AI: AI & ML Development (LangChain/Graph, LlamaIndex, PyTorch, MLflow) sowie Erfahrung mit LLM Foundation-/Fine Tuned Models (Open AI, Mistral, Anthropic, Hugging Face) und Vektordatenbanken (Azure AI Search, Chroma DB, PgVector)  
\- Data Architecture & Engineering: Data Warehouse/Data Integration (z.B.: Databricks, Snowflake, MS Fabric, BigQuery, Azure Synapse) sowie NoSQL Datenbanken (z.B.: Azure Cosmos DB, MongoDB, InfluxDB)  
 
*   Folgende Kenntnisse in einem oder mehreren dieser Bereiche sind ein Plus: Continuous Integration & Delivery (z.B.: Unit Testing, Jenkins, Release Management), Cloud Architekturen (z.B.: AWS, Azure, GCP - Zertifizierungen erwünscht), Big Data /In-Memory-Datenbanken (z.B.:Cloudera, Redis), Graphdatenbanken (Neo4j, Amazon Neptune, ArangoDB), Streaming Plattformen z.B. (Apache Kafka, Azure Event Hubs), Containerisierung & Orchestrierung (z. B. Docker, Kubernetes).  
 
*   Projektbezogene Mobilität, Kommunikationsstärke auf Deutsch und Englisch sowie eine hohe Kundenorientierung

## Benefits

*   Attraktive Benefits eines globalen Unternehmens
*   Zugriff auf internationales Wissen und Expertennetzwerke
*   Flexible Arbeitszeitmodelle & Homeoffice
*   Überstundenausgleich
*   Umfangreiche Trainings- und Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten
*   Zusammenarbeit mit führenden Expert:innen
*   Stetige fachliche und persönliche Weiterentwicklung

​**Die Accenture-Kultur: Hier machst DU den Unterschied**  
Deine Fähigkeiten, dein Naturell und deine Ambitionen machen dich einzigartig. Und wenn die unterschiedlichsten Talente, Stärken und Sichtweisen aufeinandertreffen, entsteht etwas Großartiges: Ideen, die in der Welt etwas bewegen. Deshalb setzen wir bei Accenture auf Diversität und freie Entfaltung. Schaffe dir ein Arbeitsumfeld, in dem du aufgehst. Mit Aufgaben, die dir am Herzen liegen. Mit einem Workload, der zu dir passt. Und mit einer Arbeitsweise, die sich an deinen Zielen orientiert. Wie du dich vernetzen, weiterbilden und persönlich wachsen willst, liegt bei dir. Es ist deine Karriere. Wir helfen dir, sie so zu gestalten, wie du es dir vorstellst. 

Neben spannenden Projekten bieten wir dir ein sehr attraktives Vergütungspaket, flexible Arbeitszeiten, ein modernes Umfeld und viele weitere zusätzliche Benefits. Du hast bei uns die Möglichkeit, basierend auf deiner individuellen Leistung aktiv dein Jahreseinkommen positiv zu beeinflussen.

Das Jahresbruttogehalt für diese Position startet, je nach Qualifikation und Erfahrung, bei 61.000 €.

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung!

tools.name: Jobs
tools.description: Start here with an employer slug (or company_id from company) to enumerate its openings; pass next_page back as page. Use category_ids from categories or this function's aggregations, city_id from company offices or aggregations. There is no keyword search on JOIN.

options.name: category_ids
options.about: JOIN category ids (filters.categoryIds); ids from categories or aggregations.categories.

options.name: city_id
options.about: JOIN city UUID (filters.placeIds); from company offices[].city_id or aggregations.cities[].city_id. Pattern: ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$.

options.name: company_id
options.about: JOIN's numeric company id (company.company_id). Exactly one of company_slug, company_id or url. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,12}$.

options.name: company_slug
options.about: The employer's slug on join.com: the segment after https://join.com/companies/ (equals company.domain in JOIN payloads), e.g. accenture, join. Case-insensitive. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,99}$.

options.name: page
options.about: 1-based page; pass next_page back here. A page past the last one is rejected as invalid_input.

options.name: page_size
options.about: Ads per page (the API accepted up to 50).

options.name: url
options.about: A pasted employer page URL https://join.com/companies/<slug>. Exactly one of company_slug, company_id or url. Pattern: ^https?://.

response.about: One page of an employer's online job ads from the candidate GraphQL API (PublicJobsList), filtered server-side by category ids and/or a city id, with per-category and per-city counts. Each ad carries id, title, status, workplace and remote type, city, country, category, employment and contract type, working terms (vacation days, weekly hours, start date, probation) and hybrid arrangement where the employer filled them in. Salary is not in the listing: read it with job.

fields.name: created_at
fields.about: ISO 8601 UTC as the API returns it.

fields.name: employment_terms
fields.about: Working terms the employer filled in; null when the ad has none.

fields.name: hybrid
fields.about: Hybrid arrangement; null unless the ad is HYBRID with details.

fields.name: id
fields.about: JOIN job id; pass to job as job_id.

fields.name: id_param
fields.about: URL segment of the ad, <last_id>-<title-slug>.

fields.name: last_id
fields.about: The numeric prefix of id_param (JOIN's lastId); also accepted by job and by https://join.com/jobs/<last_id>.

fields.name: remote_type
fields.about: For REMOTE ads: COUNTRY, REGION, ... as stated; null otherwise.

fields.name: status
fields.about: JOIN status as stated (ONLINE for a live ad).

fields.name: updated_at
fields.about: ISO 8601 UTC as the API returns it.

fields.name: url
fields.about: Public ad page https://join.com/companies/<slug>/<id_param>.

fields.about: ONSITE, HYBRID or REMOTE as stated.

tools.name: Listings
tools.description: Search kbb.com dealer and private-seller inventory for a make (optionally model and trim) within a radius of a US ZIP code, optionally filtered by year, price, maximum mileage, exterior colour and drivetrain. Returns one page of 25 listings with price, KBB Fair Purchase Price and deal rating, mileage, VIN, seller and distance, plus the total match count for pagination.

options.name: drive_type
options.about: Drivetrain group. kbb.com groups AWD and 4WD together, so awd and 4wd return the same listings (drive_type AWD4WD).

options.name: exterior_color
options.about: kbb.com exterior colour group; matches the manufacturer colour names in `exterior_color` (e.g. white matches Snowflake White Pearl Mica).

options.name: listing_type
options.about: Inventory to search: used, new, certified pre-owned, or all three. Defaults to used.

options.name: make
options.about: kbb.com make slug, e.g. toyota, honda, ford, mercedes-benz.

options.name: mileage_max
options.about: Only listings with at most this many miles on the odometer (kbb.com maxMileage filter; any ceiling, not just the site's 10,000-mile steps).

options.name: model
options.about: kbb.com model slug, e.g. camry, civic, f150, model-3. Omit for all models of the make.

options.name: page
options.about: Result page; 25 listings per page.

options.name: price_max
options.about: Highest advertised price to include, in whole US dollars; must not be below price_min.

options.name: price_min
options.about: Lowest advertised price to include, in whole US dollars.

options.name: radius_miles
options.about: Search radius in miles; 0 means nationwide. KBB pads a market's results with remote 'virtual dealer' delivery listings whose distance is not the seller's; with a non-zero radius these are excluded (count may be below page_size while total_count still includes them).

options.name: sort
options.about: Result order: relevance (KBB default), price_asc / price_desc by KBB derived price (advertised price plus fees, so advertised prices are only approximately ordered), mileage_asc, year_desc (newest model year first), distance_asc (nearest seller first), newest (most recently listed first).

options.name: trim
options.about: Trim name as shown in listings (e.g. SE, XLE, Sport Touring). Requires model.

options.name: year_max
options.about: Newest model year to include, inclusive; must not be below year_min.

options.name: year_min
options.about: Oldest model year to include, inclusive.

options.name: zip
options.about: Five-digit US ZIP code at the centre of the search. Pattern: ^[0-9]{5}$.

response.about: Search kbb.com dealer and private-seller inventory for a make (optionally model and trim) within a radius of a US ZIP code, optionally filtered by year, price, maximum mileage, exterior colour and drivetrain. reviews.text: Devious freshly made to order pizza.

owner_response.text:
Thank you for taking the time to share your experience, and especially for having supported Sforno since we opened. We are sorry that today’s visit left you and your family frustrated.

We did review the order. It was placed through Uber Eats at approximately 12:20 PM, and the pickup time transmitted to our system by Uber Eats was approximately 1:25 PM. Unfortunately, Uber Eats does not always display the same estimated time to the customer, driver, and restaurant. We have reported this issue to Uber Eats multiple times, as we have also had drivers arrive showing us pickup times different from those appearing on our system.

At Sforno, every pizza is stretched, topped, and baked to order. We do not precook pizzas or leave them sitting in boxes waiting for pickup because we want them to leave the oven as fresh as possible. Today was an exceptionally busy service, and when we realized there was confusion regarding your pickup time, our team moved your order ahead in the queue to try to help. Unfortunately, during a very busy service, there is a limit to how quickly we can produce additional pizzas without compromising their quality.

That said, regardless of the Uber Eats timing issue, we are sorry that our communication with you was not better. You should have received a clearer explanation and a more gracious response while you were waiting, and we will address that with our team.

We also encourage you to report the discrepancy in pickup times directly to Uber Eats. We have brought this issue to their attention multiple times, and customer reports may help them better understand and correct the problem.

We appreciate the many times you and your family have supported us, and we are genuinely disappointed that this experience did not reflect the hospitality we want our guests to receive.

reviews.text:
My wife and I have been coming since they opened. We’ve only had good experiences until today. Our family had an extremely unpleasant experience today. My wife placed an order for 3 pizzas on Uber Eats a little after 12pm. It stated it should be ready around 12:40. No problem, we walk around the neighborhood and come back a little after the pick up time.

When I arrived, I asked the young lady if our order is ready. She said “ooo” and just walks away with a tag. I’m standing there not knowing what happen so I assumed it’s not ready and wait outside. 1pm rolls around so I walk back into the restaurant but this time I asked the young gentleman if our order is ready. He said no but he will put our order in the front of the line.

I went back outside and wait again. 1:15 rolls around, I get a notification from Uber Eats that my food is ready. Great, I walk to the young gentleman again and show him my screen but he says it’s still not ready. He points to the young lady and she says, “Oo your order says it was supposed to be for 1:30 so it’s not ready.” Not sure how that is possible considering the app doesn’t have a delay pick up option and it notified me that my order was ready at 1:15.

I’m still patiently waiting outside at this point but now I start noticing that people who ordered in person after I showed up to pick up my order is getting their orders before me. There was a family that ordered their food after I arrived and even they commented “you’re still here?!?” after they ate and were leaving.

I go back to the young gentleman at 1:30pm and he says it’s still not ready… at this point my whole family is starving and I just want to leave. I finally pick up my food around 1:45 and in a nice way I told the gentleman that they should fix the Uber Eats communications and he says, “you should tell the owner, she is right here” and walks away.

I didn’t get a “sorry your order took so long”, just mean looks like why are you bothering me. Unfortunately we love supporting local restaurants but the service has gone way down. The pizza is decent but it doesn’t warrant close to a 2 hour wait and terrible service.

We will not be returning anytime soon and I will not be recommending this restaurant to anybody.
The pizza was delicious, freshly made and baked!
